entries.german: Erzbischof Heinrich von Mainz beurkundet, daß sein Kellner Engilhard in Amorbach über Einnahmen und Ausgaben seines Amtes1 in der Zeit vom 20. Febr. (fer. IV. ante diem b. Petri ad kath.) 1342 bis zum 17. Febr. (fer. II. ante diem b. Petri ad kath.) 1343 (ultimo suo recessu incluso) abgerechnet habe. Danach bleibt E. dem Erzbischof schuldig (remanet obligatus): an Roggen (siligine) 67 Mltr. 7 Simmer; an Hafer 102 1/2 Mltr. an Mohn (papavere) 4 Mltr. 3 Simmer; an Käsen (caseis) 84 Mltr. weniger 1 Käse (case); an Talg (sepo) 66 tal. an Heu 10 leydas. Der Erzbischof bleibt dem Kellner schuldig: an Spelt 156 Mltr. 6 S. an Geld 3 Pfd. 14 sol. 6 Heller. Zur Abrechnung waren vom Erzbischof zugezogen: die Kleriker Conrad, Scholaster von Aschaffenburg, und Johannes von Siegburg (Syberg); die Offiziate Ebirhard von Rosenberg in Dürn (Durne) und Conrad gen. Rüdt (Rude) in Starkenburg (-berg); der Kellner in Aschaffenburg Conrad Spiegel und die erzb. Notare Gerlach von Butzbach (Butspach), Heinrich Bavarus und Johannes von Lorch. Et notandum quod colonus in Celle tenetur domino in 10 Pfd. Heller de equis in messibus futuris proxime persolvendis.
entries.english: Archbishop Heinrich of Mainz certifies that his cellarer Engilhard at Amorbach has rendered accounts for revenues and expenditures of his office in the period from February 20 (Thursday before the feast of St. Peter's Cathedral) 1342 to February 17 (Tuesday before the feast of St. Peter's Cathedral) 1343 (his final departure included). Thereafter E. remains indebted to the Archbishop: in rye (siligine) 67 measures 7 Simmer; in oats 102 1/2 measures; in poppy seeds (papavere) 4 measures 3 Simmer; in cheese (caseis) 84 measures less 1 cheese (case); in tallow (sepo) 66 tal.; in hay 10 leydas. The Archbishop remains indebted to the cellarer: in spelt 156 measures 6 S.; in money 3 pounds 14 shillings 6 Heller. For the settlement, the Archbishop had summoned: the Clerics Conrad, Scholaster of Aschaffenburg, and Johannes von Siegburg (Syberg); the Officials Eberhard von Rosenberg at Dürn (Durne) and Conrad called Rüdt (Rude) at Starkenburg (-berg); the cellarer at Aschaffenburg Conrad Spiegel and the archiepiscopal Notaries Gerlach von Butzbach (Butspach), Heinrich Bavarus, and Johannes von Lorch. And it should be noted that a tenant in Celle is bound to his lord to pay 10 pounds Heller for horses to be delivered at the upcoming harvests.

facts.content: was present for the accounts of Engelhard, the Mainz cellarer at Amorbach, as an official in Dürn.
